## Overview

This PR introduces `skills/work-designer` as a general work-design assistant for reasoning about goals, requirements, architecture, contracts and design decisions. **Review** is its first work-design mode, producing an evidence-backed integration report without implementing fixes. **Revise** maintains the skill following the work-planner authoring pattern. These are its only modes.

## Changes

### Review Procedure

- **Coverage follows the project's design and implementation.**
  The procedure reads architecture and design documents, traces requirements through declarations and consumers, and derives checks from each affected branch's languages, constructs, schemas and responsibilities.
- **Findings identify the result actually reviewed.**
  The report records heads, targets, merge bases, tested combinations and proposed merge or deployment order. Revision freshness and CI checkout evidence determine whether observations still apply.
- **Missing evidence remains visible.**
  Executed checks, inspection and inference remain distinct. Skipped checks, unavailable environments and stale pairings prevent unsupported readiness claims.

### Project Configuration

- **Projects can carry their own variants.**
  `variants/<project>/VARIANT.md` owns project identity, planning settings, document homes and mode-specific configuration, with concrete invocations in its adjacent command reference. Selection uses an explicit choice or a unique repository match; unconfigured projects derive settings from their own sources.
- **Workflow-server is a supplied variant.**
  It covers engine and schema checks on `main`, definitions and walks on `workflows`, packaging on `docker`, and scripts, hooks and skills on `workspace`. The common procedures and dependencies remain general.
- **Planning is shared across modes.**
  A shared guide resolves the planning location and reuses the work's record. The selected project supplies its root and naming convention; the mode does not impose a review-specific folder name.

### Skill Maintenance

- **Revise follows the existing skill conventions.**
  Revisions use a worktree, authoritative rule homes, link and structure checks, representative walkthroughs and commit/push delivery.
- **Authoring rules preserve the skill's structure.**
  Rules precede Dependencies, core guidance names individual projects only as examples, and project configuration and shared planning each have one home.
- **Every revision verifies progressive disclosure.**
  Completion requires checking the required reading for each affected mode. Anchored links instruct agents to retrieve the selected section and its subsections, with explicit prerequisites; whole-file links identify documents whose full contents are needed. Variant identities link to each mode's configuration, and Review selects the affected branches' coverage sections.

## Test Plan

| Test | Description | Coverage | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T1 | Existing work-planner mode-summary suite: 3 tests pass, including discovery of work-designer | | ✓ |
| T2 | Skill-creator validator accepts the entry point and frontmatter | | ✓ |
| T3 | All 11 Markdown files checked for fences, bold-lead layout, command placement and exactly Review/Revise modes; all 94 local links and anchors resolve | | ✓ |
| T4 | All 33 repository source links resolve against local remote refs | | ✓ |
| T5 | Manual mode walkthroughs cover variant selection, branch-specific Review, Revise without integration coverage, bounded command and parent-section reads, required whole files, prerequisites and missing evidence | | ✓ |
| T6 | Staged diff passes whitespace validation | | ✓ |
| T7 | Two fresh-context sub-agents plan the same Docker-only review. Both use bounded command and project-configuration reads; one loads the complete variants guide, and both include unneeded conditional command sections | | Partial |
| T8 | A fresh-context Revise agent performs an isolated template-heading edit, reads only Identity/Revise project settings, and passes the validator, 3 summary tests, 94 local link/anchor checks and whitespace validation | | ✓ |

Live tests used three independent sub-agents with fresh conversation contexts at commit `0a6ac0b180370c03d6c10095aae577a003254834`. Their actual tool calls and returned content were audited without coaching them on expected reads. No run loaded a complete command catalog or the complete project variant. However, one Review run read all 402 words of `references/variants.md` when its link selected the 185-word Selection section. Both Review runs also read shell-syntax and restart command specs that this mapping-only change did not need. The second Review run and Revise run bounded variant selection correctly.

**Disclosure result: partial pass.** Section links guide live retrieval, but the current instruction does not consistently enforce minimal reads. This sample covers review planning and a small skill revision, not an executed integration review or a measured context-token saving. The template edit exists only in an isolated evaluation worktree; the PR's skill files remain at the evaluated commit. Local evidence is recorded under `.engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-10-10-1295-work-designer-live-disclosure/`. Initial validation encountered a sandbox namespace failure; the authorized retry passed.
